0: International Booker Prize is given every year for a single book translated into English and published in the UK/Ireland; the prize money (£50,000) is shared equally between author and translator.

Recent winners: 2022 Tomb of Sand (Geetanjali Shree, tr. Daisy Rockwell) - first Hindi novel; 2024 Kairos (Jenny Erpenbeck, tr. Michael Hofmann); 2025 Heart Lamp (Banu Mushtaq, tr. Deepa Bhasthi) - a Kannada short-story collection.
Wings of Fire = A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (with Arun Tiwari). Ambedkar: Waiting for a Visa, Annihilation of Caste. Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom. Obama: A Promised Land, Dreams from My Father.
Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay: Devdas, Srikanta, Parineeta. Bankim Chandra: Anandamath (Vande Mataram), Durgeshnandini. Bibhutibhushan: Pather Panchali. Michael Madhusudan Dutt: Meghnad Badh Kavya.

Kalidasa (Gupta court, Navaratna of Chandragupta II): Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Ritusamhara. Tulsidas: Ramcharitmanas (Awadhi). Valmiki: Ramayana. Ved Vyas: Mahabharata and Puranas.
Tip: match author-book pairs in groups (poets, novelists, translators); translators of award books are a frequent question.
1: Hornbill Festival - Nagaland (1-10 December, Kisama), called 'Festival of Festivals'. Wangala (100-drum festival) - Garo tribe, Meghalaya, honours Sun god Saljong. Moatsu - Ao Nagas.

Chapchar Kut - Mizoram (March, spring festival after jhum clearing; Cheraw bamboo dance). Kharchi Puja - Tripura (July, 14 deities, Old Agartala). Sarhul - Jharkhand (spring, Sal tree worship, Munda/Oraon/Ho).
Shigmo - Goa (spring; also Shishirotsav). Maghi Mela - Muktsar (Punjab) in memory of the 40 Muktas. Hola Mohalla - Anandpur Sahib. Baisakhi - Khalsa Panth foundation (1699).
Buddha Purnima = Vesak (Vaisakha full moon; birth, enlightenment, Parinirvana). Losar - Tibetan New Year (Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal). Losoong - Sikkim New Year. Saga Dawa - Sikkim Buddhist festival.
Other must-knows: Bihu - Assam; Onam - Kerala; Pongal - Tamil Nadu; Gangaur and Teej - Rajasthan; Bastar Dussehra - Chhattisgarh; Nuakhai, Rath Yatra - Odisha; Bhagoria - Madhya Pradesh.
2: Mission Shakti = umbrella scheme for women's safety and empowerment with two sub-schemes: Sambal (safety: One Stop Centres, Women Helplines, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao) and Samarthya (empowerment: PMMVY, Hub for Empowerment of Women, creches).

PM-KUSUM: Component A = 10,000 MW decentralised grid-connected solar plants on barren/fallow land; B = stand-alone solar pumps; C = solarisation of grid-connected pumps. PM-PRANAM rewards states for reducing chemical fertiliser use.

SVAMITVA (Ministry of Panchayati Raj, 2020): drone mapping of rural abadi land and Property Cards. U-WIN: digital registry for the Universal Immunization Programme. PM-ABHIM: health infrastructure (central sector + centrally sponsored parts).

PM-MITRA: 7 mega textile parks. PM-AASHA: Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PSS, PDPS, PPSS) for remunerative prices. PM-SYM: Rs 3,000/month pension after 60 for unorganised workers (income up to Rs 15,000), run through LIC. PM Jan Dhan Yojana (Aug 2014): financial inclusion. UDAN (2016): regional air connectivity with VGF.

SHRESHTA: residential education for meritorious SC students. Lighthouse Projects under GHTC-India (PMAY-U): six states, six innovative construction technologies. International Day of Forests: 21 March (2026 theme: Forests and Economies).
3: BIMSTEC (1997, Bangkok Declaration): Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand; HQ Dhaka; bridge between South and Southeast Asia; Pakistan is NOT a member (it is in SAARC).

BRICS: BRIC coined by Jim O'Neill (2001); first summit 2009; South Africa joined 2010; NDB agreed 2014. Expanded from 1 Jan 2024 (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE) and Indonesia in 2025. Intergovernmental, decisions by consensus, no binding supranational authority unlike the EU.

SCO: established 15 June 2001 (Shanghai Five was 1996); India observer 2005, full member 2017 (Astana). QUAD: India, USA, Japan, Australia; proposed 2007 by Shinzo Abe, revived 2017; informal strategic forum, not a military alliance.

World Happiness Report uses the Cantril Ladder (0-10). Largest BRICS country by area: Russia. Ruchira Kamboj: first woman Permanent Representative of India to the UN. National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL): New Delhi, under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
4: Preeti Rajak (trap shooter, Asian Games 2023 silver) became the first woman Subedar in the Indian Army (2024). Subedar is a Junior Commissioned Officer (JCO) rank; General, Colonel and Captain are commissioned ranks.

Ashwini Bhide (IAS, known as Mumbai's 'Metro Woman') became the first woman Municipal Commissioner of BMC in 2026. Dr Bobby Mukkamala: first Indian-origin President-elect of the American Medical Association (2024).

GI tag = product tied to a geographical origin (Namakkal soapstone cookware, Tamil Nadu, 2025). Petroglyph Conservation Park, Ratnagiri (Maharashtra): foundation stone laid on World Heritage Day (18 April).

Days to remember: World Environment Day 5 June, World Heritage Day 18 April, World Cultural Diversity Day 21 May. Maruti Chitampalli (d. 18 June 2025): Marathi wildlife conservationist and writer. Ratan Parimoo: art historian and teacher (MSU Baroda).
5: Four-fold classification (Natya Shastra): Tata/Tat Vadya = string (sitar, veena, sarod; pitch set by string tension and length); Sushira Vadya = wind (flute, shehnai; air column); Avanaddha Vadya = membrane percussion (tabla, mridangam, dholak); Ghana Vadya = solid idiophones (manjira, ghatam, cymbals).
Damaru: small two-headed hourglass drum that sounds when the wrist twists so knotted strings strike the heads (Shiva's instrument). Tavil, mridangam, nagara are struck directly.
Raga time theory (Samay Siddhant): Bhairav - early morning; Yaman - first quarter of night (evening); Malkauns - late night; Darbari Kanada - late night, associated with Tansen at Akbar's court.
Naatupura Paadalgal = Tamil folk songs tied to agrarian life and farming seasons (sowing, weeding, harvesting).
6: Narinder Singh Kapany: Father of Fibre Optics. IACS Kolkata (1876): Mahendralal Sircar; C.V. Raman did the Raman Effect research here. Meghnad Saha: Saha Institute; J.C. Bose: Bose Institute; P.C. Ray: Bengal Chemicals.

LVM3 (earlier GSLV Mk III) = ISRO's heaviest rocket: 2 solid boosters (S200), core stage with 2 Vikas engines (L110), cryogenic upper stage C25 powered by CE20. Carries about 4 t to GTO and 8 t to LEO. LVM3-M3 put 36 OneWeb satellites in LEO (2023); LVM3-M4 = Chandrayaan-3; LVM3-M5 = CMS-03.

SSLV: 3-stage all-solid, about 120 t lift-off mass, up to 500 kg to 500 km. PSLV: 'Workhorse' of ISRO; PSLV-C62 (EOS-N1, 2026) was its 64th flight. SCE-200 semicryogenic engine uses LOX + kerosene (Isrosene) in an oxidiser-rich staged combustion cycle.

Aditya-L1: solar observatory at Sun-Earth L1 point (launched on PSLV-C57). Aryabhata: India's first satellite, 19 April 1975, launched from the USSR. NISAR: NASA-ISRO dual-frequency (L and S band) SAR. Axiom-4 flew to the ISS.

MACE (Hanle, Ladakh): world's highest imaging Cherenkov telescope detecting high-energy gamma rays. Bharat Forecasting System: 6 km resolution weather model. Madras Hedgehog: first complete mitochondrial genome study in India.
7: Judo (founded 1882 by Jigoro Kano from Jujutsu) debuted at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics. Taekwondo is Korean (kicks), Karate is Japanese (striking), Wushu is Chinese.

Relay: baton exchange (handover) in a 20 m zone; anchor = last runner. Sprint records need tailwind not above +2.0 m/s. Michael Phelps: most Olympic golds (23). Bolt 8 golds, Carl Lewis 9, Serena Williams 4 (singles/doubles).

Basketball: 4 quarters (10 min FIBA, 12 min NBA); backboard 1.80 m x 1.05 m; rim 3.05 m high; three-pointer is a shot from beyond the arc. Badminton: lines 40 mm wide; even score serve from right court, odd from left; shots: drop (falls just over net), clear (high and deep), drive (flat), smash (steep, powerful).
Kabaddi: 7 players on court per side (12 in squad); raid = attacking move, 'cant' = continuous chant of 'kabaddi' in one breath, 'antis' = defenders.

Chess: stalemate (no legal move, not in check) = draw; checkmate = win; fork = one piece attacks two or more; en passant = special pawn capture; gambit = opening sacrifice. Chess entered the Asian Games medal events in 2006 (Doha).

Anti-doping: TUE allows a prohibited substance for a medical need with approval; RTP athletes must file whereabouts (60-minute daily window); steroids are banned; sample collection = urine/blood. NDTL is in New Delhi.

Indian firsts: Kamaljeet Sandhu - first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold (400 m, 1970); Saina Nehwal - first Olympic badminton medal (bronze, London 2012); PV Sindhu - silver 2016, bronze 2020; CWG 2010 Delhi - India's best, 2nd with 101 medals; Anupama Ramachandran - IBSF World Snooker (U-21) champion.
Terms: 'Bully' - field hockey restart; 'Double fault' - tennis; 'Dry firing' - shooting practice without live ammunition; handstand - inverted gymnastics position; cartwheel - sideways rotation.
8: Temple styles: Nagara (North India; curvilinear shikhara, sanctum under the tallest tower, usually no boundary wall or tank), Dravidian (South India; stepped pyramidal vimana, gopurams, high boundary walls, large water tank), Vesara (mixed, Deccan). Kerala temples use sloping tiled/copper roofs because of heavy monsoon rain.

Sandhara temple = has a roofed circumambulatory path (pradakshina patha) around the garbhagriha; Nirandhara = no such path; Sarvatobhadra = accessible from all four sides. Panchayatana = main shrine plus four subsidiary shrines (five in total), e.g. Dashavatara temple Deogarh, Kandariya Mahadeva Khajuraho.

Solanki (Maru-Gurjara) style: Sun Temple Modhera with Surya Kund (stepped tank with 108 miniature shrines). Dilwara Jain temples, Mount Abu: white marble with filigree-like ceilings (11th-13th century). Pancha Pandava Rathas, Mahabalipuram: five monolithic rock-cut temples of the Pallavas (7th-8th century).

Hawa Mahal, Jaipur (1799, Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, architect Lal Chand Ustad): 953 jharokhas so royal ladies could watch street life unseen. St Philomena's Church, Mysore: Neo-Gothic (inspired by Cologne Cathedral). Pondicherry French quarter: arcaded courtyards.
Veerangana Archaeological Museum, Jhansi: in memory of Jhalkari Bai, a close associate of Rani Lakshmibai in 1857.
9: Eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu; earlier Sadir/Dasi Attam; revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale, Kalakshetra), Kathak (North India; from 'katha' = story), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh; uses vachika abhinaya), Odissi (Odisha; chauka and tribhanga), Manipuri (Manipur; Raas Leela, Poloi/Kumil skirt, no harsh stamping), Sattriya (Assam; Sankaradeva, 15th century).

Dance terms: Nritta = pure rhythmic dance without meaning; Nritya = dance with expression; Natya = dramatic element; Abhinaya = expression. Mohiniyattam uses mandala/medium stance and soft lasya movements; Maibi dance - Lai Haraoba, Manipur.

Folk dances by state: Kud, Kud Dandi Nach - Jammu and Kashmir; Dollu Kunitha - Karnataka (Kuruba, Beeralingeshwara); Karagattam/Kavadi Aattam - Tamil Nadu; Lavani - Maharashtra; Garba - Gujarat (Navratri); Ghoomar - Rajasthan; Bhangra/Giddha - Punjab; Raut Nacha, Gaur Maria, Pandavani - Chhattisgarh (Teejan Bai is the famed Pandavani singer); Bagurumba - Bodo (Assam); Cheraw - Mizoram; Bhortal - Assam; Dalkhai - Odisha; Bhagoria - Madhya Pradesh; Garhwali - Uttarakhand.
Lavani is performed in nine-yard Nauvari sarees to dholki beats. Karma - tribal dance of Jharkhand/Chhattisgarh/MP. Chhai Lam - Mizoram.
10: Sahitya Akademi: Main Awards in 24 languages, Yuva Puraskar for writers under 35, Bal Sahitya Puraskar for children's literature.

National Book Critics Circle (NBCC) Awards 2026 (US critics' awards): Biography - Alex Green 'A Perfect Turmoil'; Poetry - Kevin Young 'Night Watch'; Autobiography - Arundhati Roy 'Mother Mary Comes to Me'.
Padma awards: Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan (3rd highest civilian honour) > Padma Shri. Dr K.R. Palaniswamy (Padma Bhushan): medicine / gastroenterology.
11: Economic systems: capitalist (market decides), socialist (state decides), mixed (government and market together - India). Micro = individual units (consumer, firm); Macro = aggregates (national income, inflation, budget).

Definitions: Marshall - welfare (human welfare and material requisites of well-being); Robbins - scarcity (allocation of scarce means with alternative uses); economics is the study of choice. Opportunity cost = value of the next best alternative foregone.

HDI (UNDP): health = life expectancy at birth; education = mean and expected years of schooling; income = GNI per capita (log transformed for diminishing returns). HDR 2025 top: Iceland (0.972). Basic Needs approach (ILO 1970s) targets provision of basic goods; Capability approach (Amartya Sen) stresses choices and freedoms.
Disinvestment = government selling part of its PSU shareholding; nationalisation = taking over private assets. Demographic dividend turns into a burden without jobs and education.
12: 1991 BoP crisis: India approached the IMF and World Bank, pledged gold, and launched the New Economic Policy (LPG - liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation); the exchange rate moved to a market-determined system (LERMS in 1992, full float in 1993).

GATT (1947/48) was replaced by the WTO on 1 January 1995 (Marrakesh Agreement, Uruguay Round); WTO also covers services (GATS) and IPR (TRIPS). Outsourcing = hiring outside (often foreign) firms for services.
New Development Bank (BRICS, 2014 agreement): equal voting power among founders, unlike weighted voting at the IMF and World Bank (Bretton Woods institutions).
13: Revenue budget = revenue receipts and revenue expenditure (day-to-day); Capital budget = capital receipts (loans, disinvestment) and capital expenditure (asset creation). Deficit budget suits recession (Keynesian); surplus budget suits inflation.

Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - total receipts excluding borrowings (= borrowing requirement). Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure - revenue receipts. Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments. FRBM Act 2003 institutionalised fiscal discipline.

Direct taxes: income tax, corporate tax, wealth tax (abolished 2015). Indirect: GST (1 July 2017, 'One Nation One Tax One Market'), customs, excise (subsumed). Proportional (flat) tax = same rate for all incomes; progressive = rate rises with income; regressive = burden falls more on the poor. Fiscal policy (government spending and taxes) directly affects aggregate demand; monetary policy is by RBI.
14: Law of demand: inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded (ceteris paribus). Price elasticity of demand = % change in quantity demanded / % change in price.

Inferior good: negative income elasticity. Normal good: positive. Exceptions to law of demand: Giffen goods (e.g., inferior staples like bajra) and Veblen/conspicuous goods. Substitute goods are a determinant of demand, not an exception.
15: Plans: 1st (1951-56) Harrod-Domar model, agriculture; 2nd (1956-61) Mahalanobis model, heavy industry; 4th (1969-74) 'growth with stability and progressive self-reliance' (14 banks nationalised); 5th (1974-78) Garibi Hatao and self-reliance, ended a year early; Rolling Plan 1978-80 (between 5th and 6th); 6th (1980-85) target 5.2%, actual 5.7%; 8th (1992-97) target 5.6%, actual 6.8%; 9th (1997-2002) target 6.5%, actual 5.4%; 10th target 8%, actual 7.6%.

Karve Committee (1955): village and small-scale industries. License Raj = licences, quotas and permits (1947-1990). New Economic Policy / New Industrial Policy, July 1991 (P.V. Narasimha Rao; Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister): LPG - liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation; industrial licensing abolished except for a few industries (alcohol, tobacco, hazardous chemicals, defence/aerospace, explosives); quantitative restrictions on imports dismantled; FDI limits raised.

PSU categories: Maharatna (2010; invest up to Rs 5,000 crore without approval), Navratna (must be a Miniratna and score 60/100), Miniratna. Retained in public sector with more autonomy. ONGC Videsh Ltd handles overseas oil and gas projects. Disinvestment = selling part of government equity.
After 1991 the services sector was the main growth driver of GDP.
16: PM-AASHA (2018) = PSS (Price Support Scheme), PDPS (Price Deficiency Payment Scheme) and PPSS (Private Procurement and Stockist Scheme). PM-KISAN gives Rs 6,000 a year; PMFBY is crop insurance; PMBJP supplies generic medicines.
PM-SYM: voluntary contributory pension for unorganised workers aged 18-40 earning up to Rs 15,000 a month; Rs 3,000 monthly pension after 60.
17: Inflation = sustained rise in the general price level (loss of purchasing power); deflation = fall in the general price level. Price control (ceilings) aims to curb inflation and protect consumers of essentials.
18: Global Innovation Index (WIPO): two sub-indices - Innovation Input and Innovation Output. NSE set up in 1992 (operations 1994) with screen-based trading and transparency; SEBI got statutory powers in 1992.

India's outsourcing edge after 1991: low wages plus a skilled English-speaking workforce. MSP protects farmers from speculators and middlemen and supports production (recommended by CACP). World Bank's B-READY replaced Ease of Doing Business; India is slated for the 2026 report. HDI is released by UNDP (Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen).
19: Narasimham Committee (1991) was the blueprint for financial sector reforms (cut SLR/CRR, deregulate interest rates, improve asset quality). Malhotra Committee (1993) - insurance; Chakravarty (1985) - monetary system; Verma (1996) - weak PSBs. Foreign investment limit in private sector banks: 74%.
20: GDP = final goods and services produced within the country; GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA); NDP = GDP - depreciation; NNP = GNP - depreciation. National income is the total value of goods and services produced.
Transfer payments = government payments without goods or services in return (pensions, welfare, subsidies). Output gap = actual GDP - potential GDP. Services sector contributes more than 50% of GVA.
21: Inter-State Council: Article 263, set up in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission recommendation; promotes Centre-State coordination (cooperative federalism).

Finance Commission: Article 280, constituted by the President every 5 years; recommends sharing of net tax proceeds between Union and States (vertical) and among States (horizontal), plus grants-in-aid.

CAG: Article 148, audits Union and State accounts. Girish Chandra Murmu became the 14th CAG in August 2020 (earlier first LG of Jammu and Kashmir UT). Article 261 - full faith and credit; Article 267 - Contingency Fund.
22: DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36-51), non-justiciable. Article 44 - Uniform Civil Code.

Fundamental Duties: Part IV-A, Article 51A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the Swaran Singh Committee; 10 duties originally, 11th added by the 86th Amendment (2002). 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights.
23: Three emergencies: National (Article 352 - war, external aggression, armed rebellion), State / President's Rule (Article 356), Financial (Article 360, never declared). Article 365 - failure to follow Union directions can lead to Article 356.

During a National Emergency Parliament can legislate on State List (Article 250); Article 19 is suspended automatically on war/external aggression (Article 358); other rights by Presidential order (Article 359) but never Articles 20 and 21 (44th Amendment).

Article 3 laws (new states, boundary changes) need only a simple majority and are not amendments under Article 368 (Article 4). Amendments to federal features need special majority plus ratification by half the states.
First Amendment (1951) added Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule; I.R. Coelho case (2007): Ninth Schedule laws after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review.
24: Right to Equality: Articles 14-18 (14 equality before law; 15 no discrimination; 16 public employment; 17 abolition of untouchability; 18 abolition of titles except military and academic).
Right to Freedom: Articles 19-22. Against Exploitation: 23-24 (Article 24 - no child labour below 14 in hazardous work). Freedom of Religion: 25-28. Constitutional Remedies: Article 32.

Article 12 defines State; Article 13 - laws inconsistent with FRs are void; Doctrine of Eclipse (Article 13(1)): pre-constitutional laws are dormant, not dead, and revive if the conflict is removed. Article 33 - Parliament can restrict FRs of armed forces. Right to Property is now Article 300A (legal right).
25: Three new criminal laws replaced IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) 2023.

BNS: mob lynching (Section 103(2), group of 5 or more, murder on grounds of race, caste, community etc.); organised crime (Section 111); terrorism (Section 113); community service as a punishment for petty first offences; Section 69 - sexual intercourse by deceitful means or false promise to marry.

BNSS: Zero FIR can be filed at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction; e-FIR. BSA: oral evidence must be direct (Section 55); electronic records are primary evidence if authenticated (Section 63); applies to courts-martial but not affidavits or arbitrators.
Regulating Act 1773: Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings), Supreme Court at Calcutta. Pitt's India Act 1784: Board of Control, double government.
26: 73rd Amendment (1992): Panchayati Raj, Part IX, 11th Schedule (29 subjects), three-tier structure. 74th Amendment: urban local bodies, Part IX-A, 12th Schedule (18 subjects). 61st Amendment lowered voting age to 18; 86th made education a Fundamental Right (Article 21A).
27: Article 254: Doctrine of Repugnancy - Union law prevails over State law on Concurrent List subjects, except where the State law has Presidential assent (Article 254(2)).

Article 256: State executive power must ensure compliance with Parliament's laws; Union can give directions. Article 355: Union's duty to protect States. Article 245: territorial extent of laws. Article 262: inter-state river disputes.
India-Bhutan: 1949 Treaty of Friendship revised in 2007; India is Bhutan's largest trade partner and helps in defence and hydropower - not nuclear technology.
Uttarakhand UCC law (as per the source) excludes Scheduled Tribes. Criminal law is enforced by police (investigation) and judiciary (trial).
28: Article 105: parliamentary privileges. Article 118: rules of procedure. Article 120: language of Parliament (Hindi or English). Article 121: no discussion on the conduct of SC/HC judges except on a removal motion. Article 122: courts cannot question parliamentary proceedings. Article 210: language in State Legislatures. Article 343: Hindi in Devanagari is the Union's official language.

Article 312: Parliament can create All India Services if Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting. Article 249: Parliament can legislate on State List in national interest. Article 315: Public Service Commissions.
29: Union Executive: Part V (Articles 52-78). Article 52: there shall be a President of India. Article 53: executive power of the Union. Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President. Article 75: PM and Council of Ministers; collective responsibility to Lok Sabha.
30: Schedules: 1st - states and UTs; 2nd - emoluments of President, Governors, Speakers, judges; 3rd - forms of oaths; 4th - Rajya Sabha seat allocation; 5th - Scheduled Areas and tribes; 6th - tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; 7th - Union, State, Concurrent lists; 8th - 22 languages; 9th - laws protected from challenge (reviewable after I.R. Coelho); 10th - anti-defection (52nd Amendment, 1985); 11th - Panchayats; 12th - Municipalities.

Basic structure doctrine: Kesavananda Bharati (1973). Judicial review, federalism and secularism are part of it; the Uniform Civil Code is only a DPSP (Article 44). Parliamentary system: executive is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
31: Appeals to SC: Article 132 - constitutional matters; 133 - civil matters; 134 - criminal matters. SC is the final interpreter and guardian of the Constitution. HC judges are appointed by the President (Article 217) and take oath before the Governor (Article 219).

Landmarks: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) - third gender recognised; K.S. Puttaswamy - Right to Privacy; Vishaka - sexual harassment guidelines; Navtej Singh Johar - decriminalised homosexuality. December 2023: bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud upheld the abrogation of Article 370.
32: Article 1: India is a Union of States. Article 2: admission or establishment of new States. Article 3: new states, boundaries and names of existing states - Bill needs the President's recommendation, who refers it to the State Legislature; its views are not binding. Article 4: such laws are not Article 368 amendments (simple majority).
33: Appointments are asked as 'who became X in month Y'. Key facts from the source: GAIL CMD (March 2026) - Deepak Gupta; DG Naval Armament - B.P. Singh; Bihar CM (15 April 2026) - Samrat Choudhary; DGCA head - Vir Vikram Yadav; VCOAS (April 2026) - Lt Gen Dhiraj Seth; Secretary, Dept of Land Resources - Narendra Bhooshan; UPSC Chairman (May 2025) - Ajay Kumar, former Defence Secretary (Articles 315-323).
Tip: remember the office's parent ministry and the constitutional article, if any (UPSC - Articles 315-323; CAG - Article 148).

More appointments from the source: first woman DG of RPF - Sonali Mishra (till October 2026); Vigilance Commissioner (January 2026) - Praveen Vashistha; ITBP DG (January 2026) - Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor; BSF DG (January 2026) - Praveen Kumar; BMC Commissioner (March 2026) - Ashwini Bhide (first woman in the post); BPCL CMD (April 2026) - Sanjay Khanna.

Harivansh Narayan Singh re-elected Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha (third term, April 2026, as per the source); Rajya Sabha Chairman is the Vice President ex-officio. Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Pay Commission (constituted November 2025). Justice Surya Kant became the 53rd CJI (November 2025), succeeding Sanjiv Khanna. A.K. Balasubrahmanian took over as AERB Chairman (January 2026, as per the source); Keshavan Ramachandran became RBI Executive Director (July 2025).
CVC: set up in 1964 on the Santhanam Committee recommendation.
34: Sahitya Akademi gives awards in 24 languages (22 Eighth Schedule languages plus English and Rajasthani). Yuva Puraskar - writers under 35; Bal Sahitya Puraskar - children's literature.

Sahitya Akademi 2025 (as per the source): Padapurana (Odia poetry) - Girijakumar Baliyar Singh; Crimson Spring (English) - Navtej Sarna; Thakur Satsayie (Dogri poetry); Bharkhama (Rajasthani stories); Gujarati poetry - Yogesh Vaidya. Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2025: English - Nitin Kushalappa; Bengali - Tridib Kumar Chattopadhyay (Ekhono Gaye Kanta Daye). Yuva Puraskar Hindi - Parvati Tirkey.

International Booker Prize 2025: Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq (Kannada), translated by Deepa Bhasthi - the first Kannada-language winner. National Book Critics Circle Award 2026 Fiction (as per the source): Han Kang, We Do Not Part; Ivan Sandrof Lifetime Achievement: Frances FitzGerald.

PM Modi: Order of Makarios III (Cyprus, 16 June 2025); the Grand Commander of the Order of the Star and Key of the Indian Ocean is Mauritius's highest honour (March 2025 visit). Nipun Malhotra - disability rights; A.E. Muthunayagam - father of India's liquid propulsion (LPSC); Radhika Gupta - CEO of Edelweiss Mutual Fund.
35: Udyam Assist Platform (UAP): digital identity for informal micro enterprises. Atal Tinkering Labs under the Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog) - 10,000 ATLs by October 2025. Stand-Up India (2016): bank loans of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. e-Shram: national database of unorganised workers, including gig and platform workers.

PM-DevINE: North-East infrastructure and social projects (Budget 2022-23). PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - subsidy Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW plus Rs 18,000 for the 3rd kW = Rs 78,000 for 3 kW; 1 crore households. 11: Sectors: primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction), tertiary (services, which contribute more than half of GVA). Basic concepts: scarcity and choice, opportunity cost, production possibility frontier, microeconomics (individual units) vs macroeconomics (aggregates; Keynes). 12: Balance of Payments = record of all transactions with the rest of the world; current account (trade in goods and services, income, transfers) and capital account (FDI, FPI, loans). Balance of trade = exports of goods minus imports of goods. Current account deficit (CAD) is financed by capital inflows.

Exchange rate: fixed, floating, managed float (India since 1993; RBI intervenes). Devaluation (official reduction under fixed rate), depreciation (market fall), appreciation, forex reserves (RBI is custodian). India's major exports - petroleum products, gems and jewellery, IT services; major imports - crude oil, gold, electronics.

Deficits: revenue deficit, fiscal deficit (total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings), primary deficit (fiscal deficit minus interest payments). FRBM Act 2003 sets deficit targets.

Taxes: direct (income tax, corporate tax; burden cannot be shifted) and indirect (GST, customs, excise; burden shifted). GST launched 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment; Article 279A GST Council); CGST, SGST, IGST, UTGST; slabs 5, 12, 18, 28 percent (rationalised in 2025); Cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool.

14: Law of demand: price up, demand down (inverse); exceptions - Giffen goods, Veblen goods (prestige), expectations. Demand curve slopes downward; shifts due to income, tastes, price of related goods, population. Elasticity: Ed = percentage change in quantity / percentage change in price; elastic (Ed above 1, luxuries), inelastic (below 1, necessities), unitary.

Law of supply: price up, supply up (direct). Supply curve slopes upward; shifts due to cost of production, technology, taxes, number of firms. Equilibrium where demand equals supply; excess demand raises price, excess supply lowers price.

Market forms: perfect competition (many sellers, homogeneous product, price taker), monopoly (single seller), oligopoly (few sellers, e.g. telecom), monopolistic competition (differentiated products), monopsony (single buyer). Price discrimination in monopoly.

Utility: total and marginal utility; law of diminishing marginal utility (Gossen); consumer surplus (Marshall); indifference curve (Hicks and Allen). Costs: fixed, variable, marginal; economies of scale.
Tip: sketch the shifts in demand and supply once; most questions are conceptual.

20: Concepts: GDP at market price, GDP at factor cost, GVA = GDP minus indirect taxes plus subsidies; GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad; NNP = GNP - depreciation; NNP at factor cost = National Income. Per capita income = national income / population. Real GDP (constant prices) vs nominal GDP; GDP deflator.

Methods: production (value-added) method, income method, expenditure method (C + I + G + (X - M)). NSO (National Statistical Office) under MoSPI releases estimates; base year 2011-12; Central Statistics Office was merged with NSSO in 2019 to form NSO. First National Income Committee 1949 (P.C. Mahalanobis); V.K.R.V. Rao pioneered estimates.

Sectors contribution: services over 50 percent, industry around 25-28 percent, agriculture about 15-18 percent of GVA. India is among the top five economies by nominal GDP (about fourth or fifth in recent IMF estimates) and third by PPP.

22: DPSP (Part IV, Articles 36-51): borrowed from the Irish Constitution; non-justiciable but fundamental in governance (Art. 37). Socialist: Art. 38 (social order), 39 (equal pay for equal work; resources), 41 (work, education), 42 (humane conditions, maternity relief), 43 (living wage), 43A (workers in management), 47 (nutrition, health, prohibition). Gandhian: Art. 40 (village panchayats), 43 (cottage industries), 46 (SC/ST), 47, 48 (cow protection). Liberal-intellectual: Art. 44 (Uniform Civil Code), 45 (early childhood care), 48A (environment), 49 (monuments), 50 (separation of judiciary), 51 (international peace).

Amendments: 42nd (1976) added 39(f), 39A (free legal aid), 43A, 48A; 44th (1978) added 38(2); 86th (2002) changed Art. 45 and made Art. 21A education a Fundamental Right for ages 6-14; 97th (2011) Art. 43B cooperatives.

Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A): added by 42nd Amendment (1976) on Swaran Singh Committee recommendation; originally 10, 11th added by 86th Amendment (2002) - duty of parents to provide education to child aged 6-14. Borrowed from the USSR constitution. Non-justiciable. Includes respecting the Constitution, flag, anthem, protecting environment and sovereignty, developing scientific temper.
Relationship: Minerva Mills case (1980) - harmony between Fundamental Rights and DPSP is the basic structure; Kesavananda Bharati (1973) - Parliament cannot alter basic structure.
Tip: remember Art. 44 (UCC), 40 (panchayats), 48 (agriculture and animal husbandry), 51 (international peace).
23: Emergency provisions (Part XVIII, Art. 352-360): National Emergency (Art. 352) on war, external aggression or armed rebellion (since 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance'); declared by the President on written advice of the Cabinet; Parliament must approve within one month by special majority; imposed in 1962, 1971, 1975. State Emergency/President's Rule (Art. 356) - failure of constitutional machinery; approval within two months; maximum 3 years; S.R. Bommai case (1994) made it subject to judicial review. Financial Emergency (Art. 360) - never declared.

Effects of National Emergency: Fundamental Rights under Art. 19 automatically suspended during war/external aggression; Art. 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment); Lok Sabha term can be extended by one year at a time; Centre can legislate on State List.

Important amendments: 1st (1951) - Ninth Schedule, reasonable restrictions on speech; 7th (1956) - reorganisation of states; 24th - Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights; 25th; 31st; 42nd (1976) 'mini Constitution' - added Socialist, Secular, Integrity to Preamble; 44th (1978) - Right to Property removed from Fundamental Rights (Art. 300A); 52nd (1985) - anti-defection, Tenth Schedule; 61st (1989) - voting age 18; 73rd and 74th (1992) - Panchayats and Municipalities; 86th (2002); 91st (2003) - size of Council of Ministers limit 15 percent; 101st (2016) - GST; 102nd (2018) - NCBC constitutional status; 103rd (2019) - 10 percent EWS reservation; 104th - SC/ST seats in Lok Sabha extended to 2030; 105th; 106th (2023) - Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, one-third reservation for women.
Amendment procedure: Art. 368; simple majority, special majority, or special majority plus ratification by half of the states.
Tip: memorise amendment number, year and subject as a table.
24: Part III, Articles 12-35 (Magna Carta of India; borrowed from USA). Six rights: Right to Equality (14-18), Right to Freedom (19-22), Right against Exploitation (23-24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29-30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). Right to Property was removed in 1978 and made a legal right under Art. 300A.

Equality: Art. 14 equality before law (Irish) and equal protection (American); 15 no discrimination; 16 equality in public employment; 17 abolition of untouchability; 18 abolition of titles. Freedom: Art. 19(1) six freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession); 20 protection in conviction; 21 life and personal liberty (Maneka Gandhi case widened it); 21A education for 6-14; 22 protection against arbitrary arrest.

Exploitation: Art. 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour; 24 bans child labour in factories/mines below age 14. Religion: Art. 25 conscience and religion; 26 manage religious affairs; 27 no tax for promotion of a religion; 28 religious instruction. Cultural: 29 protection of minorities, 30 minorities to run educational institutions.

Remedies (Art. 32 - Dr Ambedkar's 'heart and soul'): five writs - Habeas Corpus (produce the body), Mandamus (we command), Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto (by what authority). Supreme Court (Art. 32) and High Courts (Art. 226).

Key cases: Kesavananda Bharati 1973 (basic structure), Golaknath 1967, Maneka Gandhi 1978, Right to Privacy fundamental (Puttaswamy 2017), Navtej Johar 2018 (Section 377 decriminalised), Shreya Singhal 2015.
Tip: remember which rights are available only to citizens (Art. 15, 16, 19, 29, 30).

41: Buddhism: founder Gautama Buddha (born 563 BCE at Lumbini, Sakya clan of Kapilavastu; father Suddhodana, mother Mahamaya); Mahabhinishkramana (renunciation) at 29; enlightenment at Bodh Gaya under the Pipal tree at 35; first sermon at Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana); death (Mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagar, 483 BCE. Five vows (Panch Mahavrata): ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha and brahmacharya (added by Mahavira). Triratnas: right faith, knowledge, conduct.

42: Founder Sri Gupta; Ghatotkacha; real founder Chandragupta I (319-320 CE; Gupta era began 319 CE; married Kumaradevi of Licchavi). Samudragupta (335-380 CE) - 'Napoleon of India' (V.A. Smith); Allahabad (Prayag) Pillar inscription by Harishena; performed Ashvamedha; coins show him playing the veena. Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (380-415 CE): defeated Shakas of Malwa, took title Vikramaditya; Chinese traveller Fa-hien visited; Navratnas incl. Kalidasa; Iron Pillar at Mehrauli.

Administration: king with title Maharajadhiraja; provinces (bhuktis) under uparikas; districts (vishayas) under vishayapatis; villages under gramika; land grants to Brahmins (agraharas) strengthened feudalism. Coins: dinaras (gold). Trade guilds, flourishing but less overseas trade.

Culture - Golden Age: literature (Kalidasa, Vishakhadatta, Shudraka, Vishnu Sharma - Panchatantra); science (Aryabhata - Aryabhatiya, Varahamihira - Brihat Samhita, Brahmagupta); medicine (Dhanvantari, Sushruta); architecture (Dashavatara temple at Deogarh, Bhitargaon brick temple); art (Ajanta paintings, Sarnath Buddha); Nalanda mahavihara. Puranas compiled; Smritis (Narada, Katyayana).
Tip: remember rulers in order and the foreign travellers; inscription authors are favourite questions.

South: Sangam age - Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas; Sangam literature (Tolkappiyam, Silappadikaram, Manimekalai); Karikala; Senguttuvan. Trade with Rome (Arikamedu).

Crops: wheat, barley, peas, sesame, mustard, cotton; animals: humped bull, buffalo, sheep, dog; no iron or horse; copper and bronze used. Dancing girl statue (bronze), bearded priest (steatite).

46: Early Vedic (Rigvedic) period c. 1500-1000 BCE: Sapta Sindhu region; Rigveda has 1,028 hymns in 10 mandalas (family mandalas 2-7, oldest; 10th includes Purusha Sukta; Gayatri Mantra in Mandala 3 addressed to Savitri); society tribal and pastoral; Rajan (king), Jana, Vish, Gram; Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha assemblies; cow main wealth (gavishti); deities Indra, Agni, Varuna, Soma, Rudra; Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna) on the river Parushni (Ravi) where Sudas defeated; Saraswati is the holiest river; Sindhu the most mentioned.

Satapatha Brahmana, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

Vedas: Rigveda (hymns), Samaveda (melodies; origin of Indian music), Yajurveda (sacrificial formulas; Krishna and Shukla), Atharvaveda (spells; medicine). Vedangas: Shiksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Chhandas, Jyotisha. Upanishads: 108 (Mundaka contains 'Satyameva Jayate').

Straits: Bosphorus, Gibraltar, Hormuz, Malacca (India-Indonesia), Bering; canals: Suez (Mediterranean-Red Sea), Panama. Islands: Greenland largest; Andaman and Nicobar; Lakshadweep (coral); Majuli (largest river island, Brahmaputra).

Indian geography: Rann of Kachchh, Chilika (largest brackish lagoon), Loktak (Manipur; Keibul Lamjao floating national park), Sambhar (largest inland saline lake), Vembanad (longest lake of Kerala), Lonar (meteorite crater), Pulicat; dams: Bhakra Nangal (highest gravity), Tehri (highest in India), Hirakud (longest), Sardar Sarovar, Nagarjuna Sagar.

Climate regions of the world (Koppen): tropical, dry, warm temperate, cold snow, polar. Global belts and winds. Geography of continents: Asia (largest), Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.
Tip: remember record holders (largest, longest, highest).
85: Indian monsoon: caused by differential heating of land and sea; shift of ITCZ; Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau; Somali jet; Jet stream; El Nino (weakens monsoon) and La Nina (strengthens); Indian Ocean Dipole. Onset at Kerala about 1 June; withdrawal from Rajasthan in September. Seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb; western disturbances give rain in Punjab; retreating monsoon), Summer (Mar-May; loo; Kalbaisakhi in Bengal; Mango showers in Kerala), Southwest monsoon (Jun-Sep; 75 percent of rainfall), Retreating monsoon (Oct-Nov; Tamil Nadu rain from northeast monsoon).

Rainfall: Mawsynram (Meghalaya) is the wettest place in the world; Cherrapunji; Western Ghats windward side 250+ cm; Rajasthan (west) lowest below 25 cm; Rain shadow area of Deccan. Branches: Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch. IMD in Pune (Mausam Bhawan, Delhi); 1875 founded. Normal rainfall about 88 cm.
Climate types in India: tropical monsoon, tropical savanna, semi-arid steppe, hot desert, humid subtropical, mountain climate. Cold weather phenomena: western disturbance (Mediterranean).
Agriculture link: kharif (June-October; rice, maize, cotton), rabi (October-March; wheat, gram, mustard), zaid (summer).
Tip: remember wind systems and phenomena names.
86: First national park of India: Jim Corbett (Uttarakhand; 1936 as Hailey National Park). Largest national park: Hemis (Ladakh). Kaziranga (Assam; one-horned rhino; UNESCO), Manas (Assam; tiger), Sundarbans (West Bengal; Royal Bengal tiger; mangroves), Gir (Gujarat; Asiatic lion; only home), Ranthambore (Rajasthan; tiger), Bandipur and Nagarhole (Karnataka), Periyar (Kerala; elephants), Silent Valley (Kerala; lion-tailed macaque), Keibul Lamjao (Manipur; Sangai deer), Bandhavgarh and Kanha (Madhya Pradesh; tiger), Kuno (cheetah), Dachigam (hangul, Kashmir), Great Himalayan (Himachal), Nanda Devi, Valley of Flowers (Uttarakhand), Namdapha (Arunachal; four big cats), Balphakram (Meghalaya), Simlipal (Odisha), Bhitarkanika (saltwater crocodile).

Concepts: National parks (no human activity; Section 35 of the Wildlife Protection Act 1972), sanctuaries (limited activity), conservation and community reserves, biosphere reserves, tiger reserves (NTCA), elephant reserves, Ramsar sites. India has about 106 national parks and over 500 sanctuaries. Mammals: tiger (national animal), Asiatic lion, rhino, elephant (heritage animal), snow leopard, red panda.
Birds: Peacock (national bird); Keoladeo Ghana (Bharatpur; UNESCO), Chilika and Nalsarovar for migratory birds; Salim Ali Sanctuary; Great Indian Bustard (Rajasthan; critically endangered).
Tip: remember each park with its state and flagship animal.
87: Northern plains: formed by alluvial deposits of Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra; divisions - Bhabar (pebbles at foothills), Terai (marshy), Bhangar (old alluvium) and Khadar (new alluvium, fertile), Delta region. Punjab-Haryana plains (Doab), Ganga plain, Brahmaputra plain. Rajasthan plain: Thar desert (Marusthali, Bagar), Luni river, salt lakes Sambhar, Didwana, Pachpadra; barchans; Aravallis (oldest fold mountains) Guru Shikhar highest.

Ganga system: Gangotri -> Bhagirathi + Alaknanda at Devprayag -> Ganga; tributaries Yamuna (Yamunotri), Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi (sorrow of Bihar), Son, Chambal, Betwa; length about 2,525 km; Ganga Delta largest. Brahmaputra: Tibet (Tsangpo) -> Dihang -> Brahmaputra; Majuli island. Indus: Indus Water Treaty 1960 with Pakistan (India has Ravi, Beas, Satluj).
Coastal plains: Western (Konkan, Karnataka coast, Malabar) and Eastern (Coromandel, Northern Circars, Utkal); Chilika, Pulicat, Vembanad lakes.

Islands: Andaman and Nicobar Islands in Bay of Bengal (572 islands; Port Blair capital; Barren Island volcano; Saddle Peak highest; Ten Degree Channel; Indira Point), Lakshadweep in Arabian Sea (coral atolls, 36 islands; Kavaratti capital; Eight Degree and Nine Degree Channels), Minicoy, Majuli, New Moore Island, Sriharikota, Elephanta. Mumbai from Salsette.
Tip: remember the divisions and channels.
88: Peninsular plateau of India: oldest landmass, part of Gondwana; main divisions - Central Highlands (Malwa plateau, Bundelkhand, Baghelkhand, Chotanagpur plateau - 'Ruhr of India'), Deccan plateau (Maharashtra plateau with black cotton soil, Karnataka plateau, Telangana plateau). Boundaries: Aravallis, Vindhyas, Satpura, Maikal range, Mahadev hills, Western Ghats (Sahyadri; 1,600 km; Anamudi highest), Eastern Ghats (discontinuous; Mahendragiri, Nilgiri meeting point, Palkonda, Javadi hills).

Western Ghats: Sahyadri, Nilgiri, Anamalai, Cardamom hills; passes Thal Ghat (Mumbai-Nashik), Bhor Ghat (Mumbai-Pune), Palghat gap (Kerala-Tamil Nadu); UNESCO site 2012; origin of Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri. Eastern Ghats: Odisha to Tamil Nadu. Deccan Traps (volcanic lava, basalt, black soil, regur).

Rock: Archean granite and gneiss; Dharwar system; Vindhyan system; Gondwana coal; Deccan Trap. Plateaus: Chotanagpur (rich minerals), Malwa, Mewar, Telangana, Dandakaranya. Satpura: Dhupgarh highest at Pachmarhi.
Importance: minerals (coal, iron, bauxite), hydropower, forests, black soil for cotton.
Tip: remember plateau names, hills and passes.
89: East-flowing (Bay of Bengal; deltas): Mahanadi (Chhattisgarh/Odisha; Hirakud), Godavari (Dakshin Ganga; Nashik/Trimbak; longest peninsular river about 1,465 km; Polavaram), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar; Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam), Kaveri (Talakaveri, Karnataka; Sivasamudram, Mettur, Grand Anicut; Srirangapatna), Pennar, Subarnarekha. West-flowing (Arabian Sea; estuaries): Narmada (Amarkantak; Sardar Sarovar; Dhuandhar falls; rift valley), Tapti (Betul), Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni, and short Western Ghats rivers (Sharavati, Periyar, Bharatapuzha, Pamba).

Tributaries: Godavari - Pranhita, Indravati; Krishna - Tungabhadra, Bhima, Koyna; Kaveri - Hemavati, Bhavani, Amaravati; Mahanadi - Tel, Ib. Peninsular rivers are seasonal, rain-fed, have fixed courses and form deltas in the east; the Narmada and Tapti flow west through rift valleys.
River-linking: Ken-Betwa link (2021 agreement), Par-Tapi-Narmada. Inter-state disputes: Cauvery, Krishna, Godavari, Mahadayi, Narmada water disputes; Inter-State Water Disputes Act 1956; Tribunals.
Major cities on rivers: Kolkata (Hooghly), Hyderabad (Musi), Vijayawada (Krishna), Nashik (Godavari), Tiruchirappalli (Kaveri).
Tip: remember origin, mouth, tributaries and major dams.
90: Rocks: Igneous (granite - intrusive, basalt - extrusive), Sedimentary (sandstone, limestone, shale, coal; fossils), Metamorphic (marble from limestone, slate from shale, quartzite from sandstone, gneiss from granite, anthracite from coal). Rock cycle. Minerals: quartz, feldspar, mica; Mohs hardness scale (diamond 10, talc 1).

Continents: Asia (largest), Africa (second largest, Sahara, Nile), North America, South America, Antarctica (coldest, highest average elevation, no permanent population), Europe, Australia/Oceania (smallest). Largest country Russia; largest island Greenland; highest Everest; lowest Dead Sea.

Oceans: Pacific (largest and deepest; Mariana Trench 11,034 m (Challenger Deep)), Atlantic (second; S-shaped; Mid-Atlantic Ridge; Sargasso Sea, no coast), Indian (only named after a country; warmest), Arctic (smallest, shallowest), Southern. Ocean salinity average 35 parts per thousand (Dead Sea highest; Lake Van); Seawater composition NaCl. Tides: spring (new and full moon) and neap (quarter Moon); highest tides in the Bay of Fundy.
Ocean relief: continental shelf, slope, abyssal plain, trench, seamount, guyot, mid-ocean ridge. Coral reefs: Great Barrier Reef (largest), Lakshadweep atolls. Marine resources: nodules, oil, fish.
Tip: remember ranks (largest, deepest) and rock transformations.
91: Soil types: Alluvial (most widespread, Northern Plains, rich in potash, poor in phosphorus; Khadar and Bhangar), Black/Regur (Deccan; cotton; moisture retentive; formed from basalt), Red and Yellow (Peninsular; iron oxides), Laterite (Western Ghats, Meghalaya; leached; tea, coffee, cashew), Arid/Desert (Rajasthan), Forest/Mountain, Saline, Peaty. Soil erosion: gully, sheet; conservation: contour ploughing, terracing, shelter belts. Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); Soil Health Card scheme.

Cropping: Kharif (rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, jute, groundnut, soybean), Rabi (wheat, barley, gram, mustard, pea), Zaid (watermelon, cucumber). Major crops: rice (West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab - top), wheat (Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana), sugarcane (Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra), cotton (Gujarat, Maharashtra), jute (West Bengal; golden fibre), tea (Assam, West Bengal, Nilgiri), coffee (Karnataka, Kodagu), rubber (Kerala), millets (Rajasthan, Karnataka), pulses (Madhya Pradesh), oilseeds, spices (Kerala), horticulture. India is the largest producer of milk, pulses and spices, second in rice, wheat and sugarcane.

Farming types: subsistence, commercial, plantation, shifting cultivation (jhum in the northeast; podu in Andhra; Bewar in Madhya Pradesh), terrace, dry farming, organic farming (Sikkim first fully organic state). Irrigation: canals (Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh), wells and tube-wells (Northern Plains), tanks (Tamil Nadu, Andhra), drip and sprinkler. Revolutions: Green, White, Blue, Yellow, Golden, Pink.
Fertilisers: urea (nitrogen), DAP, NPK, potash; Neem-coated urea. MSP and e-NAM, FCI.
Tip: match crop with state, season and soil.
92: Sun: star, 99.8 percent of mass; temperature surface about 5,500 C, core about 15 million C; hydrogen and helium; light reaches Earth in 8 minutes 20 seconds; sunspots; photosphere, chromosphere, corona. Planets in order: Mercury (nearest, smallest), Venus (hottest, rotates east to west, Earth's twin; morning and evening star), Earth (blue planet; only life; 1 moon), Mars (red planet; 2 moons Phobos and Deimos; Olympus Mons highest volcano), Jupiter (largest; 90+ moons; Great Red Spot), Saturn (rings; Titan; lowest density), Uranus (rotates on its side; coldest atmosphere), Neptune (farthest). Dwarf planets: Pluto (reclassified 2006), Ceres, Eris, Haumea, Makemake.

Moon: Earth's only natural satellite; distance about 384,400 km; one side always visible (synchronous rotation); light takes about 1.3 s; phases (lunar month 29.5 days); lunar eclipse at full moon, solar eclipse at new moon; first landing Apollo 11 (1969) Neil Armstrong; Chandrayaan-3 south pole 2023.

Others: asteroids (belt between Mars and Jupiter), comets (Halley every 76 years; next 2061), meteors (shooting stars), meteorites; Galaxy: Milky Way (spiral); Andromeda nearest large galaxy; Big Bang theory (Lemaitre; 13.8 billion years); light year = 9.46 trillion km; Pole star; constellations (Ursa Major/Saptarishi, Orion). Universe stars: Sirius brightest, Proxima Centauri nearest after Sun.
Earth data: age about 4.5 billion years; Escape velocity 11.2 km/s; Earth's rotation 24 h, revolution 365.25 days (leap year every 4 years).
Tip: remember planets in order with superlatives.
93: Railways: first train Bombay to Thane 16 April 1853 (34 km); Indian Railways is the largest network in Asia (about 68,000 km route); 17 zones; headquarters Delhi; Railway Board; electrification near 100 percent; fastest train Vande Bharat; Gatimaan Express; longest run Vivek Express (Dibrugarh to Kanyakumari); longest platform Gorakhpur; highest railway station Ghum; Konkan Railway; Mumbai Metro; Delhi Metro (2002); Dedicated Freight Corridors; High-speed rail (Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train); Chenab Bridge (highest rail arch bridge in the world).

Roads: National Highway Authority of India (NHAI, 1988); NH-44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is the longest; Golden Quadrilateral (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata); North-South and East-West corridors; Bharatmala; Atal Tunnel Rohtang (longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft); Zojila tunnel; Border Roads Organisation (BRO, 1960) builds roads in border areas; PM Gram Sadak Yojana (2000); expressways such as Yamuna, Delhi-Mumbai; Pamban bridge.

Waterways: National Waterways Act 2016 (111 waterways); NW-1 Ganga (Haldia-Allahabad); NW-2 Brahmaputra; NW-3 West Coast Canal (Kerala); Inland Waterways Authority (IWAI, 1986). Ports: 13 major ports - Kandla (Deendayal; tidal port), Mumbai, JNPT (Nhava Sheva; largest container), Mormugao, New Mangalore, Kochi, Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar), Chennai, Ennore (Kamarajar), Visakhapatnam (deepest), Paradip, Haldia, Kolkata; Vadhavan (new major port); Sagarmala.

Air: Airports Authority of India (1995); Indira Gandhi International (Delhi; largest); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj (Mumbai); Kempegowda (Bengaluru); UDAN scheme (2016); Air India (Tata, 1932; nationalised 1953; re-privatised 2022); DGCA; Noida Jewar airport. Pipelines: oil and gas pipelines (HVJ).
Tip: remember firsts, lengths and authorities.
94: Pressure belts: Equatorial low, Subtropical highs, Subpolar lows, Polar highs. Planetary winds: Trade winds (towards equator; north-east in the northern hemisphere), Westerlies (Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Screaming Sixties), Polar easterlies. Coriolis force deflects winds right in the northern hemisphere and left in the southern. Local winds: Loo (India), Chinook (Rockies; snow eater), Foehn (Alps), Mistral (France), Sirocco (Sahara), Harmattan (doctor), Bora, Santa Ana, Brickfielder.

Ocean currents: warm - Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Kuroshio, Brazil, Agulhas, East Australian; cold - Labrador, Humboldt/Peru, Benguela, California, Canary, West Australian, Oyashio. Gyres: clockwise in the north, anticlockwise in the south. Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic. Where warm and cold currents meet: rich fishing grounds (Grand Banks near Newfoundland, Dogger Bank, Japan). El Nino: warming off Peru; La Nina cooling.

Cyclones: tropical cyclones (hurricane in the Atlantic, typhoon in the Pacific, cyclone in the Indian Ocean, willy-willy in Australia); eye is calm; direction anticlockwise in the northern hemisphere, clockwise in the southern; forms over warm sea above 26.5 C. Bay of Bengal is more cyclone-prone; names assigned by region (WMO/ESCAP panel); IMD; Cyclone names such as Amphan, Fani, Tauktae, Yaas, Biparjoy, Michaung, Remal, Dana. Temperate cyclones (frontal), tornado (USA), anticyclones.
Jet streams: high-altitude westerly winds; Subtropical jet stream influences Indian monsoon.
Tip: memorise local winds with regions.
95: Countries and capitals: Afghanistan - Kabul, Australia - Canberra, Bangladesh - Dhaka, Bhutan - Thimphu, Brazil - Brasilia, Canada - Ottawa, China - Beijing, Egypt - Cairo, France - Paris, Germany - Berlin, Indonesia - Jakarta (new capital Nusantara), Iran - Tehran, Iraq - Baghdad, Israel - Jerusalem, Japan - Tokyo, Kenya - Nairobi, Nepal - Kathmandu, Pakistan - Islamabad, Russia - Moscow, Saudi Arabia - Riyadh, South Africa - Pretoria (executive), Sri Lanka - Colombo, Turkey - Ankara, UAE - Abu Dhabi, UK - London, USA - Washington DC.

Rivers: Nile (Egypt; longest), Amazon (largest by volume), Yangtze (longest in Asia), Mississippi-Missouri, Danube (Europe), Rhine, Volga (Europe longest), Congo, Mekong, Euphrates and Tigris (Mesopotamia), Indus, Ganga. Deserts: Sahara (largest hot), Gobi, Thar, Arabian, Kalahari, Atacama (driest), Namib, Antarctica (cold). Mountains: Himalayas, Andes (longest), Alps, Rockies, Urals (Europe-Asia), Atlas, Appalachians.

Physical features: Mount Everest, Aconcagua (highest in S. America), Kilimanjaro (Africa), Mont Blanc, Elbrus (Europe), Mount Denali (North America), Vinson Massif (Antarctica), Kosciuszko (Australia); largest lake Caspian; deepest Baikal; Gulfs - Persian, Mexico; Seas - Mediterranean, Black, Red, Caspian, Dead, Arabian, South China. Straits and canals as in the Miscellaneous notes.

Boundary lines: 38th parallel (North and South Korea), 17th parallel (old Vietnam), 49th (USA-Canada), Durand Line, Radcliffe Line, McMahon Line, Maginot Line, Siegfried Line, Oder-Neisse; Line of Actual Control (India-China).
Tip: use map practice - mark each country with its capital and neighbours.
96: Layers: Troposphere (0-12 km; weather phenomena; temperature decreases 6.5 C per km; contains 75 percent of mass; tropopause), Stratosphere (to 50 km; ozone layer; jet aircraft; stratopause), Mesosphere (to 80 km; coldest; meteors burn), Thermosphere (hot; ionosphere reflects radio waves; aurora; satellites), Exosphere (merges into space). Composition: nitrogen 78 percent, oxygen 21 percent, argon 0.93 percent, CO2 about 0.04 percent. Ozone layer filters UV-B.

Insolation, heat budget, albedo; greenhouse effect; Temperature inversion; Humidity (absolute, relative), clouds (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbus), Precipitation types (rain, snow, sleet, hail; convectional, orographic/relief, cyclonic/frontal). Isotherms, isobars, isohyets.
Air masses and fronts: cold front, warm front, occluded front. Weather vs climate (long-term average). Pressure: barometer (millibar), 1013.25 mb at sea level; winds blow from high to low pressure.
Climate change: global average temperature rise about 1.1 C since pre-industrial; carbon cycle; ozone hole over Antarctica; acid rain; urban heat island; Smog and fog differ; Air quality index.
Tip: memorise layers and their features.
